name: L4981AD013TR
title: L4981A, L4981B: average-current-mode power factor correction controllers
summary: The L4981A and L4981B control a boost pre-regulator that draws near-sinusoidal current from the mains, reaching a power factor up to 0.99 and keeping line current distortion under 5 %, from 85 to 265 V mains with no range switch. They use average current mode PWM with a multiplier, line (VRMS) and load (LFF) feedforward, a 5.1 V ±2 % reference brought out, a totem-pole gate driver for an external MOSFET or IGBT, soft start, overvoltage and overcurrent protection, and an undervoltage lockout with hysteresis and a programmable turn-on threshold. The L4981A runs at a fixed frequency and can be synchronised; the L4981B modulates its frequency with the line voltage. Both come in DIP20 and SO20.

pins.name: P-GND
pins.function: Power ground.

pins.name: IPK
pins.function: Peak current limit input. On the L4981A one resistor from this pin to the sense resistor sets the limit against an internal current source; a second resistor from this pin to VREF (pin 11) makes the limit more accurate. On the L4981B the limit is set by a two-resistor divider between the sense resistor, this pin and the reference voltage.

pins.name: OVP
pins.function: Overvoltage protection input. A resistor divider from the boost output feeds it; when it exceeds the internal 5.1 V (typ) threshold the output peak voltage is limited.

pins.name: IAC
pins.function: Current input that follows the instantaneous rectified line voltage. The multiplier turns it into the current amplifier reference.

pins.name: CA-OUT
pins.function: Output of the current amplifier; an external RC network on it sets the current loop gain.

pins.name: LFF
pins.function: Load feedforward voltage input: scales the multiplier output with the load so the converter answers load steps faster. It works best between 1.5 V and 5.3 V. Tie it to VREF (pin 11) when the function is unused.

pins.name: VRMS
pins.function: Line RMS input: a DC level that tracks the RMS line voltage, made by low-pass filtering the rectified line; it corrects the loop for line changes. Best range 1.5 V to 5.5 V. Tie it to VREF (pin 11) when unused.

pins.name: MULT-OUT
pins.function: Multiplier output, and also the non-inverting input of the current amplifier; a high-impedance node. Keep it above -0.5 V.

pins.name: ISENSE
pins.function: Inverting input of the current amplifier. Keep it above -0.5 V.

pins.name: S-GND
pins.function: Signal ground.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: 5.1 V (typ) reference output, ±2 %, internally current limited, able to source up to 10 mA.

pins.name: SS
pins.function: Soft-start capacitor to ground. An internal 100 µA (typ) source charges it; an internal MOS transistor discharges it during overvoltage and undervoltage lockout.

pins.name: VA-OUT
pins.function: Output of the voltage error amplifier; the RC network on it shapes the voltage loop.

pins.name: VFEED
pins.function: Inverting input of the voltage error amplifier, fed from the boost output through a resistor divider.

pins.name: P-UVLO
pins.function: Programmable undervoltage lockout input. A divider from the supply to ground on this pin sets the turn-on threshold.

pins.name: SYNC
pins.function: L4981A only. Synchronisation pin, CMOS logic compatible. As an input it takes a rectangular wave; as an output it gives a rectangular clock pulse train to synchronise other devices.

pins.name: FREQ-MOD
pins.function: L4981B only. Frequency modulation current input: a resistor from the rectified line to this pin modulates the oscillator frequency. Grounded, the frequency is fixed by ROSC and COSC.

pins.name: ROSC
pins.function: A resistor to ground sets the fixed current that charges COSC.

pins.name: COSC
pins.function: A capacitor to ground sets the switching frequency.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply input.

pins.name: GDRV
pins.function: Gate driver output: a totem pole of bipolar and DMOS transistors, giving peak currents above 1 A to drive a MOSFET or IGBT.

notes: Both packages share one pinout. The L4981A and L4981B differ only at pin 16 (SYNC on the A, FREQ-MOD on the B).

circuits.title: Figure 9A: L4981A power factor corrector, 200 W
circuits.description: A 200 W boost PFC stage from 88 to 254 VAC to a 400 V bus. The bridge output feeds the 0.9 mH boost inductor, switched by Q1 through D1 into C2. R17A and R17B feed IAC with a current that follows the rectified line; R6A, R6B, R7 with C7, C8 and R8 form a two-pole filter giving VRMS a DC level proportional to the line RMS. RS senses the inductor current in the return: R3 ties MULT-OUT and R4 ties ISENSE across it, and R5 with C3 compensate the current amplifier. R11 to the sense resistor and R21 to VREF set the peak current limit on IPK. R1A, R1B and R2 feed VFEED, with R12 and C9 compensating the voltage loop; R9A, R9B and R10 set the 442 V overvoltage point on OVP. LFF is tied to VREF. C4 and R16 set the oscillator, C6 the soft start. At start-up Q2, biased from the line through R19A and R19B and clamped by the 22 V zener DZ, charges C11 to supply VCC; once running the inductor auxiliary winding, through R14, C10, D3 and D4, takes over. Q3, driven from VREF through R20, connects the R22/R23 divider that programs the UVLO threshold. D2 and R13 drive the gate of Q1, and C12, D5 and R18 form the drain snubber.

circuits.title: Figure 19: demo board circuit, VO = 400 V, PO = 360 W
circuits.description: A 360 W boost PFC demo board giving a 400 V bus from 88 to 264 Vac, for either the L4981A or the L4981B. Two STM12NM50 MOSFETs in parallel switch the 0.5 mH inductor L1. The inductor current reaches the bus through D4 and a 2.5 Ω NTC; the MOSFET drains hang off the inductor through the 3 µH L2, which with D7, C14 and R18 returns its energy to the bus, and D5 with the 48 V transil D6 clamps the inductor node. Cs, Q4 and R25 snub the drains. VCC comes at start-up from the line through R11 and R12 and in operation from L1's auxiliary winding through the bridge B2, R14, the 18 V zener Dz1 and C10. R4, R5, C2, C3 and R2 filter the rectified line into VRMS; R6 and R7 feed IAC. R9 (50 mΩ) senses the current in the return, with R3 to MULT-OUT, R13 to ISENSE and R8 with C6 compensating the current amplifier; R1 and R10 divide between the sense resistor and VREF to set the current limit on IPK. R19, R20 and R21 feed VFEED, R16 and C11 compensate the voltage loop, and R22, R23 and R24 set the overvoltage point. C9 and R15 set the oscillator, C12 the soft start, C13 decouples VREF, LFF is tied to VREF and P-UVLO is left open. With an L4981B, RAux1 and RAux2 from the rectified line drive FREQ-MOD; TP1 sits on that pin.

equations.name: Multiplier output current with LFF tied to VREF

operation.text: The chip runs a boost converter in average current mode. The multiplier combines the line-shaped current into IAC, the voltage error amplifier output and the VRMS and LFF inputs into a current reference on MULT-OUT; the current amplifier forces the averaged inductor current to follow it, so the line current stays sinusoidal without slope compensation. Average current mode gives low noise sensitivity.

The L4981A works at a fixed frequency and its pin 16 is a sync input/output. The L4981B modulates its frequency: a resistor from the rectified line into FREQ-MOD lowers the oscillator frequency as the line voltage rises, so it is lowest at the peak of each half cycle (Figure 17), which helps reduce the input filter. With pin 16 grounded the B runs at the fixed frequency set by ROSC and COSC.

ROSC (pin 17) to ground sets the constant current that charges COSC (pin 18); COSC to ground sets the switching frequency. The ramp runs from a 1.15 V (typ) valley through 5 V (typ) valley to peak. COSC = 1 nF with ROSC = 24 kΩ gives 100 kHz typ. Figure 18 gives the frequency for other values.
SYNC is CMOS logic compatible. Used as an input it takes a rectangular wave; used as an output it delivers rectangular clock pulses, 0.8 µs wide typ, that synchronise other devices.

VRMS (pin 7) takes a DC level proportional to the line RMS voltage, made by low-pass filtering the rectified line, and compensates the loop for line voltage changes; it works best between 1.5 V and 5.5 V. LFF (pin 6) scales the multiplier output with a voltage that follows the load, for faster response to load steps; it works best between 1.5 V and 5.3 V. Either input goes to VREF when not used.

The overcurrent comparator on IPK (pin 2) has a threshold within ±30 mV. On the L4981A an internal 85 µA (typ) current source serves pin 2, so one resistor between pin 2 and the sense resistor sets the trip current; a second resistor from pin 2 to VREF improves precision. On the L4981B pin 2 leaks under 5 µA and the limit is set by a divider between the sense resistor, pin 2 and VREF.

OVP (pin 3) compares a divided sample of the boost output with an internal 5.1 V (typ) threshold, with 250 mV (typ) hysteresis, limiting the output peak voltage. In overvoltage the soft-start capacitor is discharged.
The soft-start ramp is a capacitor from SS (pin 12) to ground, charged by a 100 µA (typ) internal source. An internal MOS transistor discharges it in overvoltage and in undervoltage lockout.

Before start-up the chip draws 0.3 mA (typ). It turns on at 15.5 V and off at 10 V (typ). A divider on P-UVLO (pin 15), R22 from VCC and R23 to ground, lowers the turn-on threshold: 220 kΩ with 33 kΩ gives 12 V typ, and Table 1 and Figure 16 give other pairs. VCC is clamped by an internal zener of 25 V typ, and in absolute maximum terms the supply is self-limiting with ICC up to 50 mA, within the package dissipation.
VREF (pin 11) is 5.1 V typ, ±2 %, internally current limited (30 mA typ short-circuit current) and can supply up to 10 mA to external circuits.

GDRV (pin 20) is a totem pole of bipolar and DMOS transistors giving peak currents above 1 A to a MOSFET or IGBT; its high level is clamped at 16 V typ. Into 1 nF it rises in 50 ns and falls in 30 ns typ.
MULT-OUT (pin 8) and ISENSE (pin 9) are high-impedance inputs and must not be taken below -0.5 V.
P-GND (pin 1) is the power ground and S-GND (pin 10) the signal ground.

Figures 9A and 9B are 200 W, 400 V designs: fSW 80 kHz for the A and 80 to 92 kHz for the B, 2.53 A maximum RMS line current, overvoltage at 442 V and 6.2 A peak current limit. Figure 19 is a 360 W demo board; Tables 2 and 3 give its measured power factor of 0.987 to 0.999 and efficiency of 0.92 to 0.964 from 88 to 264 Vac.
